Build one source rule for a recipe

Source: R/recipe.R
recipe_rule.Rd

Constructs a single rule for one of a recipe's eleven source slots, for use with recipe_new. Rules within a slot combine by OR.

Usage

recipe_rule(...)

Arguments

...

Named rule fields, e.g. icd10 = c("I21", "I22"), match = "prefix".

Value

A ukbflow_recipe_rule object (a named list).

Details

recipe_rule only captures the fields you give it; which fields are legal depends on the slot the rule is assigned to, so validation happens in recipe_new where that slot is known. The legal fields per slot are:

selfreport

field ("noncancer"/"cancer"), regex

hes, hes_icd9, opcs

icd10/icd9/opcs, match, position

gp_read2, gp_ctv3

read2/ctv3, match

death

icd10, match, cause

first_occurrence, algorithm

field

cancer_registry, cancer_registry_icd9

subtype, icd10/icd9, histology, behaviour

match is "prefix"/"exact"/"regex", position is "any"/"main", and cause is "any"/"primary"/"secondary". Omitted modifiers fall back to the corresponding derive_* default rather than being written out.

Fields that are scalar per rule – regex for selfreport, field for first_occurrence and algorithm – expand into one rule per element when given a vector, so a definition built from several First Occurrence fields is still a single call.

Examples

recipe_rule(icd10 = c("I21", "I22"), match = "prefix")
#> $icd10
#> [1] "I21" "I22"
#> 
#> $match
#> [1] "prefix"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "ukbflow_recipe_rule" "list"               
recipe_rule(field = "noncancer", regex = c("^angina$", "^heart attack$"))
#> $field
#> [1] "noncancer"
#> 
#> $regex
#> [1] "^angina$"       "^heart attack$"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "ukbflow_recipe_rule" "list"
